finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role. requireRole() returns a boolean and does not throw, and its result is discarded, so any caller (including a user with no roles) can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Admin.wipe(User u, String tenant) parameters: u and tenant come from the request. Precondition: the caller reaches the POST /tenants/{t}/wipe handler with any User object. The authentication code that builds User is not in this repo.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (destructive, irreversible tenant wipe)

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point, no precondition check
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called as a statement; its boolean return value is ignored
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws (Javadoc at line 13 says so explicitly)
repo.wipe(tenant) executes regardless of the role check result

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16): returns boolean, does not enforce. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22): would throw, but wipe() does not call it. Export at line 32 uses checkRole correctly, so the defect is local to wipe(). No other guard visible in this repo. Caveat: the HTTP/auth layer is out of scope, so whether an unauthenticated caller can reach this method is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and never throws. Its result is discarded as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs unconditionally. checkRole (lines 18-22) throws, but wipe() does not call it; export() at line 32 does. No other guard exists in this repo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: wipe() at src/Admin.java:25-28 discards requireRole's boolean at line 26 and calls repo.wipe at line 27 for any User, including one with no roles. The only caveat is that the HTTP/auth layer, which is outside this repo, could still block unauthenticated callers from reaching the POST /tenants/{t}/wipe handler; that does not stop an authenticated low-privilege user from wiping a tenant.

finding.claim: Role checks are not scoped to the target tenant. User carries a global Set<String> of roles with no tenant binding, so an OWNER of tenant A may be able to wipe or export tenant B by passing a different tenant id. This applies to both wipe (line 26) and export (line 32).
finding.source: tenant parameter of export(User u, String tenant) and wipe(User u, String tenant) (src/Admin.java:25, 31), taken from the request path. Precondition: the caller holds OWNER on at least one tenant.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33 (cross-tenant data export) and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (cross-tenant wipe)

trace.note: record User(String name, Set<String> roles): no tenant field, so roles are not bound to a tenant
export(User u, String tenant) accepts an arbitrary tenant id
checkRole(u, "OWNER") checks only that the role exists, not that it applies to this tenant
repo.export(tenant) runs for the attacker-chosen tenant

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) checks role membership only. No tenant-membership or tenant-ownership check exists in this file. Severity depends on how the caller builds the roles set; if roles are already per-tenant upstream, this finding is not valid. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE, needs the caller code to confirm.

verdict.guard_found: For export (src/Admin.java:32), checkRole (lines 18-22) throws SecurityException when the role is missing, so the result is enforced, though it checks only role membership, not tenant. For wipe (src/Admin.java:26), requireRole (lines 14-16) returns a bool that is discarded, so no check runs at all. No tenant-binding check exists anywhere in the repo, which contains only src/Admin.java.
verdict.reason: The trace misdescribes wipe: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, a bool-returning function whose result is discarded, so wipe has no role enforcement at all, not a tenant-scoping gap as claimed. The export claim (src/Admin.java:32-33) depends on whether roles are tenant-scoped upstream, which the repo does not contain, so the tenant-scoping part is unverifiable, but the finding as written is inaccurate.
